hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3)
scope: IN: endosomal or endolysosomal luminal pH/acidity, and lysosomal pH as a neighbouring compartment (a contrary or related result); acidity probes of those compartments (ratiometric dextran/transferrin pH probes, LysoTracker, LysoSensor, pHrodo when read as acidity); regulators on the path to endosomal pH (NHE6/NHE9 expression or function, V-ATPase, the HDAC-CREB-NHE6 axis) measured or manipulated in an APOE4 context. OUT: mitochondrial/mitophagy pH, mTOR or other signalling readouts, whole-proteome changes, cell viability, amyloid or cargo uptake not read as compartment acidity.

rows.Finding description: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia showed no significant difference in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH, reported as approximately 5.15, with three wells per group.
rows.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH in human iPSC-derived microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Untreated baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH measured ratiometrically with dextran polymers labeled with pH-sensitive ApHID and pH-independent Alexa 647; three wells per group, nine imaging frames per well. Donor age and AD status were not specified for this isogenic pair.
rows.Data location: Fig 3G, untreated APOE33 vs untreated APOE44

rows.Finding description: After organoid-debris challenge, human isogenic APOE33 microglia acidified from about pH 5.15 to 5.05 (*** vs untreated APOE33 in Fig 3G), whereas APOE44 microglia did not acidify significantly (ns vs untreated APOE44); debris-treated APOE44 late-endosomal/lysosomal pH was about 0.08 units higher than debris-treated APOE33 (about 5.13 vs 5.05, read from Fig 3G), with three wells per group.
rows.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (impaired challenge-induced late-endosomal/lysosomal acidification in human iPSC-derived microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Organoid-debris challenge followed by ratiometric late-endosomal/lysosomal pH imaging using dextran-conjugated ApHID and Alexa 647; three wells per group, nine frames per well. Challenge duration and donor age/AD status were not specified in the supplied text.
rows.Data location: Fig 3G, APOE33+debris vs APOE44+debris (also each vs its untreated genotype)

rows.Finding description: In the female UCI5 isogenic pair, organoid-debris challenge lowered APOE33 microglial late-endosomal/lysosomal pH (about 5.30 to 5.24, * vs untreated in Fig 7M) but raised APOE44 pH (about 5.29 to 5.40, *** vs untreated); debris-treated APOE44 pH was about 0.17 units higher than debris-treated APOE33 (about 5.40 vs 5.24, read from Fig 7M), with three wells per group.
rows.Finding quote: Upon challenge with organoid debris, UCI5 APOE44 iMG lysosomes failed to mount an adaptive acidification response and instead shifted toward alkalinization (Figure 7M).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (impaired adaptive endolysosomal acidification, with challenge-induced alkalinization reported in APOE4 microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from the additional female UCI5 APOE33/APOE44 isogenic pair, assayed untreated and after organoid-debris challenge. Late-endosomal/lysosomal acidity measured ratiometrically with dextran polymers labeled with ApHID and Alexa 647; three wells per group, 25 frames per well. Donor age, AD status, and challenge duration were not specified in the supplied text.
rows.Data location: Fig 7M, UCI5 (33)+debris vs UCI5 (44)+debris (also each vs its untreated genotype)

rows.Finding description: Proteomics comparing human isogenic APOE44 with APOE33 microglia found significant downregulation of 53 of 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, without separately reporting the V-ATPase subset.
rows.Finding quote: Of the 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, 53 were significantly downregulated in APOE44 iMG, supporting lysosomal impairment (Figure S3D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower abundance of a combined lysosomal hydrolase/V-ATPase protein set)
rows.Experimental system: Proteomic analysis of human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Identified lysosomal proteins were assessed for differential abundance. This measures a protein set containing acidification regulators rather than luminal pH itself.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig S3D; numerical counts reported in main Results

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes showed significantly higher lysosomal LysoTracker mean intensity than isogenic APOE3 astrocytes (about 41 vs 55 a.u. read from Fig 3G, ~35% higher), consistent with increased acidic-compartment staining but without a measured luminal pH difference.
rows.Finding quote: We also observed that ApoE4 increased the intensity of LysoTracker, which is positively associated with lysosomal ac- tivity (Figure 3G
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal LysoTracker intensity in human astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human AG10788 AD-donor iPSC-derived APOE4 astrocytes and CRISPR-corrected isogenic APOE3 astrocytes; donor female, age 87; serum withdrawn at least 4 days; LysoTracker Red DND-99 staining at 250 nM for 30 minutes, fixation, confocal imaging, and mean signal-intensity quantification; no ratiometric pH calibration.

rows.Finding description: Four-day methyl-β-cyclodextrin treatment lowered elevated LysoTracker intensity in APOE4 astrocytes; cholesterol is a downstream intervention target and LysoTracker intensity is an indirect acidity readout.
rows.Finding quote: We further observed restoration of lysosomal activity, as indicated by the mitigated intensity of LysoTracker after lysosomal cholesterol depletion (Figures 4D and 4F).
rows.Finding summary: (cholesterol depletion in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower lysosomal LysoTracker intensity)
rows.Experimental system: Human AG10788 AD-donor iPSC-derived APOE4 astrocytes, female donor age 87; methyl-β-cyclodextrin versus untreated APOE4 cells for 4 days; confocal quantification of lysosomal LysoTracker intensity; no calibrated luminal pH measurement.
rows.Data location: Fig 4F, APOE4 plus methyl-β-cyclodextrin versus untreated APOE4
